sections.title: 一、詞彙題（占10分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第1題至第10題為單選題，每題1分。

questions.stem: The bus driver often complains about chewing gum found under passenger seats because it is ______ and very hard to remove.
Jesse is a talented model. He can easily adopt an elegant ______ for a camera shoot.
In order to draw her family tree, Mary tried to trace her ______ back to their arrival in North America.
Upon the super typhoon warning, Nancy rushed to the supermarket—only to find the shelves almost ______ and the stock nearly gone.

sections.title: 二、綜合測驗（占10分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第11題至第20題為單選題，每題1分。

groups.passage:
In certain forests, when you look up you will see a network of cracks formed by gaps between the outermost edges of tree branches. It looks like a precisely engineered jigsaw puzzle, each branch growing just perfectly so it almost, [[11]], touches the neighboring tree. This beautiful phenomenon is called crown shyness.
Scientists have been discussing crown shyness since the 1920s, proposing [[12]] explanations for the phenomenon. Some researchers point out that as trees often grow close together, treetops can easily collide and break when swayed by the wind. In order to protect their branches from breakage, trees maintain “shyness gaps”—spaces large enough to prevent them from touching their neighbors.
Other scientists suggest that plants, like animals, [[13]] resources—nutrients, water, space, and light. In forested areas with thick tree crowns, there is intense struggle for these resources. Gaps in the treetops resulting from crown shyness may allow trees to increase their [[14]] light and enhance photosynthesis. Additionally, by having branches that do not touch those of their neighbors, trees may be able to limit the spread of leaf-eating insects, and potentially also the transmission of diseases from tree to tree. [[15]] decades of investigation, there is no consensus on exactly what causes the beautiful and mysterious phenomenon of crown shyness.

Gravity has been at the top of the science agenda since the start of Mars missions. In the earlier days of space travel, scientists tried to overcome the force of gravity so that a rocket could shoot [[16]] Earth’s pull in order to land humans on the moon. Today, they are more interested in how reduced gravity affects the astronauts’ [[17]] condition.
Our bodies have evolved to exist within Earth’s gravity (1 g), not in the weightlessness of space (0 g) or the microgravity of Mars (0.3 g). When on Earth, we have more fluids in our lower body because they are pulled down by Earth’s gravity. However, with the absence of gravity in the outer space, our body fluids [[18]], shifting toward the upper body and the head. As a result, the astronauts have swollen, puffy faces, very much resembling that of the round-headed Charlie Brown in the famous comic strip. This “Charlie Brown effect” will be more [[19]] when the astronauts go on their Mars missions, which will take about three years to complete, much longer than missions to the moon. Moreover, the effect is often [[20]] space motion sickness, headaches, and nausea. Such a syndrome is considered the top health risk for the astronauts, and scientists are still trying to figure out how it may be prevented.

sections.title: 三、文意選填（占10分）
sections.instructions: 說明：第21題至第30題為單選題，每題1分。

groups.passage:
Water makes up more than half of our body weight. To sustain this amount of fluid in our bodies, plain water is considered our best choice, for it contains no sugar and no calories. Yet, is water always the healthiest drink we can [[21]]? Well, it depends on who and where we are, and what we’re doing.
Obviously, a physically [[22]] person with an outdoor job under the sun will need to drink more fluid than a desk-bound person who lives and works in an air-conditioned place. But there’s more to it than that. When a person sweats, he loses water and salt, so he needs to replace both. Replacing lost fluid with just plain water means the body has too much water and not enough salt. To [[23]] things out, the body will get rid of water by producing urine. For this reason, milk can actually be more [[24]] than drinking water. Milk naturally contains salt and lactose, a sugar which the human body needs in small amounts to help stimulate water [[25]]. Coconut water, which contains salt and carbohydrates, is also more functional than water at restoring and maintaining a normal fluid [[26]] after exercise.
For the average person, however, water remains a very good [[27]] for keeping hydrated—if you know how to drink it. The secret is: Never wait until the body is telling you you’re thirsty, since there must already have been significant changes in your body for it to eventually [[28]] your consciousness. At that point, it might be well past the best moment to take in fluid. Also, drinking a lot of liquid in one go can cause more water to [[29]] the body quickly and come out as urine. To [[30]] this, you need to drink water throughout the day to maintain your hydration levels.

sections.title: 四、篇章結構（占8分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第31題至第34題為單選題，每題2分。

groups.passage:
Have you ever thought of “coloring” the names of the days of the week? When you listen to someone speaking, do you see a rainbow of colors? Or perhaps Mozart’s music tastes like an apple pie to you? If so, it is very likely that you have synesthesia.
Synesthesia is a condition in which people’s senses intermix. In some cases, people with synesthesia may experience colors when they hear, read, or even think of letters and numbers. In others, words can trigger a real sensation of taste on their tongue.
[[31]] In the early 1990s, however, scientists noticed that synesthetic colors do not change over time. When asked what color is evoked by a letter or number, synesthetic people would persistently give the same answer even if tested months or years apart. [[32]] The most compelling support, however, comes from brain scans, which show that color processing areas in the brain light up when these people listen to certain words.
Is synesthesia genetically inherited or acquired after birth? Scientists agree that synesthesia has a genetic basis, because it frequently runs in families. But an actual synesthesia gene (or genes) has not been identified yet. [[33]] For example, the flavors people with taste-word synesthesia experience are usually childhood flavors, such as chocolate or strawberries. Also, people with color-music synesthesia more often than not have had early musical training.
Once thought to be extremely rare, synesthesia is now found to affect about one to four percent of the population. [[34]] As is often observed, most of us tend to associate lower notes with darker colors and higher notes with brighter colors. Researchers further point out that in most people synesthesia is active only during the first months of their infancy, while this ability remains forever in certain individuals.

options_bank.A: This consistency serves as a proof that synesthesia is real.
options_bank.B: Meanwhile, environmental influences seem to shape a person’s synesthesia.
options_bank.C: People with synesthesia used to be accused of making their experiences up.
options_bank.D: Some studies even show that people may all be synesthetic to some degree.

environmental influences → For example, childhood flavors / early musical training

groups.passage:
When did people first experience the joy of the hula hoop? Although the term did not emerge until the 18th century, toy hoops twirled around the waist, limbs, or neck can be traced back to ancient times. As early as 1000 BC, Egyptian children played with hoop toys of dried grapevine. They threw, jumped, and slung them around their bodies as we do today. They also struck them with sticks to roll them down the road. Hoop rolling was also popular in ancient Greece. Their hoops, often made of metal, were not merely toys for Greek children but served as exercise devices as well.
In the 14th century, hoops were popular as a form of recreation in Great Britain. The craze for hoops even resulted in dislocated backs and heart attacks, according to medical records. The term “hula,” however, did not enter the English language until the 1700s, when British sailors first witnessed hula dancing in the Hawaiian Islands. Though no hoops were used, the movements of the ritual dances looked very similar to those in hooping. Thus “hula” and “hoop” came together, resulting in the term “hula hooping.”
Hoops spun their way through the cultures of pre-colonial America as well. Often considered as representing the circle of life, hoops featured prominently in the ritual dances of Native Americans. Dancers used small reed hoops as symbolic representations of animals such as eagles or snakes. With very rapid movements, they used the hoops to construct the symbolic forms around their bodies.
The hula hoop gained international popularity in the late 1950s, when a plastic version was successfully marketed by California’s Wham-O toy company. Twenty-five million plastic hoops were sold in less than four months. The hula hoop “fad” is still going strong today.

groups.passage:
When you enjoy your morning cup of tea, you are probably not aware that those tea leaves can mean injury, or even death, for Asian elephants roaming Indian tea gardens.
In the Indian state of Assam, growing numbers of tea farms are destroying the Asian elephant’s habitats and endangering their population. Much of the forest land where tea is grown in Assam is flat and thus farmers must dig drainage trenches to prevent water from accumulating and hurting the shrubs. The trenches, however, can be death traps for the elephants. Since the elephants need to use tea plantations as landmarks when navigating forests, they almost inevitably have to move through the farms. Moreover, because there are fewer humans around, pregnant females often use tea-growing areas as safe shelters to give birth. But baby elephants, not used to negotiating rough ground, may easily fall into the trenches and get hurt; and once injured, they might not be able to climb out. When mothers try to dig their babies out, both may be trapped and smothered by thick mud. Furthermore, elephants are known to resist leaving their sick or dying behind, and a herd may linger at a trench with a trapped baby for hours, reluctant to move on until all hope is lost.
Is it possible for elephants to coexist with the prosperous tea business? Elephant Friendly Tea is an organization that takes the initiative to make <u>it</u> possible. The organization encourages consumers to choose brands that take precautions to protect elephants and has set up a certification program to reward tea growers who are doing it right. Until now, only smaller tea brands have been certified, but awareness is growing. The organization believes that people may be motivated to buy elephant-friendly brands when they know more about the risk tea can pose to these endangered animals.

groups.passage:
Situated off the coast of Tanzania and washed by the warm, clean waters of the Indian Ocean, Zanzibar is a tropical archipelago comprised of several scattered islands. This popular beach destination is now famous for its white sand beaches, slender palms, and turquoise seas. But few people know that in the past, control of Zanzibar meant access to unimaginable wealth.
From ancient times, Zanzibar has been a trading hotspot, thanks to its location on the trade route between Arabia and Africa. Traders from Asia had already visited the islands 900 years before the arrival of its first permanent settlers from the African mainland (around 1000 AD). In the 8th century, Persian merchants built settlements here, which grew over the next four centuries into their trading posts. Between the 12th and 15th centuries, trade increased between Arabia, Persia, and Zanzibar, bringing the archipelago both wealth and power.
During the Age of Exploration, commerce in Zanzibar quickly boomed, largely due to the rise of the spice trade. At the close of the 15th century, Europeans’ craze for spices gave rise to the Spice Route, a network of sea lanes joining Europe with the Far East, where most spices came from. In 1498, Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama made the first sea voyage to India, via the southernmost tip of Africa. In 1499, he arrived at Zanzibar, an archipelago sitting at the crossroads of the Spice Route. The islands soon attracted traders from different lands. Hundreds of ships sailing the Spice Route docked here, bringing spices and goods for transaction, and Zanzibar became one of the biggest trading centers in the world.
Since the 16th century, Zanzibar has come under the rule of the Portuguese, the Arabians, and then the British, each leaving a mark on the place. The paths of various religions also crossed here: Muslims have lived peacefully with Christians and Buddhists on the islands for centuries. The unique cultural intersections, scented with the aroma of cloves, vanilla, and cinnamon floating in the air, give these jewels on the Indian Ocean an amazing charm that goes far beyond tropical beach fun.

groups.passage: Even if you’re not a vegetarian, there’s a good chance you’ve heard of plant-based meat. These meat substitutes are often advertised as beneficial for the environment. But do the customers really like them? Read the following chatroom discussions about GreenBurger, a product using alternative-meat patties.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: Olivia
passage_parts.text: That’s a firm NO! I tried one when I was a prep cook for Next Level Burgers…tasted awful, just like mashed peas gone to rot.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Smith
passage_parts.text: I haven’t tried them. I just don’t see the point. They are heavily processed with more calories and sodium than meat and are more expensive too! Unless you are a strict vegetarian and eschew meat for ethical reasons, meat is surely a better deal.

passage_parts.label: C
passage_parts.title: Mika
passage_parts.text: Not really. It tastes too much like actual meat. If I wanted to eat a dead cow, I would go for real burgers. Being vegan means I try to stick to plant food. But this is just not something that will ever interest me.

passage_parts.label: D
passage_parts.title: Thomas
passage_parts.text: GreenBurger just tastes “beany” to me, so I think that whatever form it comes in, it works better in recipes that would usually contain beans, such as in a rice bowl (as ground meat substitute). That being said, I’m definitely a carnivore and prefer meat, but I don’t see anything wrong with choosing one of the fakey-fakey meaty things once in a while—just for a change.

passage_parts.label: E
passage_parts.title: Rico
passage_parts.text: I finally tried one last week. It didn’t taste that bad, but I was surprised to find it had 40 more calories than the meat version! Isn’t it supposed to be a healthy choice?

passage_parts.label: F
passage_parts.title: Linda
passage_parts.text: I liked it fine. I did NOT like the price, though. Hopefully that will come down. I’m trying to eat less beef.

passage_parts.label: G
passage_parts.title: Ablo
passage_parts.text: Yes! My whole family does. We’ve been mostly vegan 90% of the time for the last 6 years and we cannot thank GreenBurger enough! Especially when a burger craving hits…a GreenBurger does the trick. I’ve tried all kinds of vegan “burgers,” and GreenBurgers are closer to what I’m looking for. In fact, I can have them every day—vegan or not!

passage_parts.label: H
passage_parts.title: Alexander
passage_parts.text: Well, they taste good if you add plenty of spices and sauces. Good for you? No, not at all. They’re highly processed and contain no vegetables. They also contain a very large amount of processed coconut oil, which is even worse than lard. It’s a killer for sure if eaten regularly. So why risk your life?

questions.stem: 避免衝突、確保世界和平應該是所有人類追求的目標。
questions.answer: To avoid conflicts and ensure world peace should be the goal pursued by all human beings.
accepted_answers: Avoiding conflicts and ensuring world peace should be the goal pursued by all human beings.
questions.scoring_notes:
中譯英部分與過去相同，考生須將兩個中文句子譯成正確、通順且達意的兩個英文句子，兩題各占4分，共計8分；原則上是每個錯誤扣0.5分，相同的錯誤只扣一次。第一句「歷史一再證明，戰爭會造成極為可怕的災難。」，所評量的標的字詞如：「一再」應譯為 time and again/repeatedly，「戰爭」為 wars，「造成」為 cause/lead to，「極（為）」為 extremely，「可怕的」為 terrible/horrible，「災難」則為 disasters。第二句「避免衝突、確保世界和平應該是所有人類追求的目標。」，「避免」譯為 avoid，「衝突」為 conflicts，「確保」則為 ensure，「世界和平」則為 world peace，「追求」應譯為 pursue，「目標」goal。所評量的字詞大致都以詞彙表一至四級詞彙為主，考生只要句法使用正確，且注意用字、拼字的正確性，應能得到不錯的分數。
（一）滿分參考答案（大括號內為可替換寫法）：
{To avoid / Avoiding} conflicts and {ensure / ensuring} world peace should be the goal pursued by all human beings.
（二）評分原則：
1. 本大題總分8分，每小題滿分4分。
2. 每個錯誤扣0.5分，各部分獨立，扣完為止。
3. 相同之拼字錯誤或文法錯誤，只扣一次。
4. 句首未大寫或標點符號不妥，各扣0.5分，只扣一次。

questions.label: 英文作文
questions.stem: 提示︰隨著社群媒體的普及，表情符號（emoji）的使用也極為普遍。請參考下列表情符號，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段說明人們何以喜歡使用表情符號，並從下列的表情符號中舉一至二例，說明表情符號在溝通上有何功能。第二段則以個人或親友的經驗為例，討論表情符號在訊息表達或解讀上可能造成的誤會或困擾，並提出可以化解的方法。
questions.scoring_notes:
英文作文部分，主題為表情符號（emoji）的使用，屬於生活情境，貼近考生的生活範疇。考生須根據所提供的四張表情符號的圖片，第一段說明人們何以喜歡表情符號，並從四個表情符號中舉一至二例說明其溝通之功能；第二段則以個人或親友經驗為例，討論使用表情符號造成表達上的誤會或困擾以及化解的方法。英文作文評分重點在於內容須符合題目要求，提供充分、具體之細節，句構語法及用字適切，以及拼字與標點符號使用得當；內容充實以及語言能力表現佳應是考生得分之重要元素。請參閱本中心將於4月17日出刊的第336期《選才電子報》。
（一）評分原則：
英文作文依考生在內容、組織、文法句構、字彙拼字之表現評分，各項得分加總後給予一個整體分數（holistic score），再依總分1至20分，分為下述五等級：特優（19-20分）、優（15-18分）、可（10-14分）、差（5-9分）、劣（0-4分）。閱卷委員在仔細評閱考生的作答內容後，再依其內容是否切題、組織是否具連貫性、句子結構與文法、用字是否適切表達文意，及拼字與標點符號使用是否正確等要項，進行評分；為確保評分一致性，在試閱時，閱卷委員皆必須完全熟悉及理解各分項的評分標準（分項說明詳見表一）。字數明顯不足者，扣總分1分；未分段者，亦扣總分1分。
表一、英文作文評分指標（項目／優／可／差／劣）
內容：優（5-4分）主題（句）清楚切題，並有具體、完整的相關細節支持。／可（3分）主題不夠清楚或突顯，部分相關敘述發展不全。／差（2-1分）主題不明，大部分相關敘述發展不全或與主題無關。／劣（0分）文不對題或沒寫（凡文不對題或沒寫者，其他各項均以零分計算）。
組織：優（5-4分）重點分明，有開頭、發展、結尾，前後連貫，轉承語使用得當。／可（3分）重點安排不妥，前後發展比例與轉承語使用欠妥。／差（2-1分）重點不明、前後不連貫。／劣（0分）全文毫無組織或未按提示寫作。
文法、句構：優（5-4分）全文幾無文法、格式、標點錯誤，文句結構富變化。／可（3分）文法、格式、標點錯誤少，且未影響文意之表達。／差（2-1分）文法、格式、標點錯誤多，且明顯影響文意之表達。／劣（0分）全文文法錯誤嚴重，導致文意不明。
字彙、拼字：優（5-4分）用字精確、得宜，且幾無拼字、大小寫錯誤。／可（3分）字詞單調、重複，用字偶有不當，少許拼字、大小寫錯誤，但不影響文意之表達。／差（2-1分）用字、拼字、大小寫錯誤多，明顯影響文意之表達。／劣（0分）只寫出或抄襲與題意有關的零碎字詞。

extraction.method: python-docx 讀 Word 版題本（paper-2.docx）取段落文字與空格位置，與 pdftotext -layout 的 PDF 題本（paper-1.pdf）逐詞比對（英文字詞序列除 PDF 換行斷字「fakey-／fakey」與上標「18 th」外完全一致；中文標題、說明、中譯英與作文提示亦逐字比對一致）；Read 看 PDF 頁面影像（並以 pdftoppm 200dpi 放大裁切）確認第44題世界地圖四個圓圈位置、混合題聊天室版面與粗體、作文四個表情符號圖片；答案取自 answer.pdf（pdftotext）；混合題、中譯英、作文的參考答案與評分原則取自 scoring.pdf（pdftotext＋Read 頁面影像確認大括號與表格）；答題卷 other-1.pdf 確認第49題劃記區為 A–H；統計以 xlrd 讀 stats-1/2/3.xls 的「英文」工作表，並以程式核對：選項分析中標「*」的選項與官方答案逐題一致、單選題 P 與正確選項 T 列選答率一致、Ph／Pl 與 H／L 列正確選項一致、D＝Ph−Pl；人工校對。；查證者另以程式比對 Word 版／pdftotext 文字、xlrd 重讀三個統計檔，並以 Read 與 pdftoppm 放大檢視題本第2–12頁與評分原則第1–3頁影像。
issues: 結構核對：與 gsat-spec.json current（111學年度起現制）一致——選擇題46題62分（詞彙1–10、綜合測驗11–20兩篇各5空、文意選填21–30、篇章結構31–34每題2分且選項(A)–(D)共4個、閱讀35–46三篇各4題每題2分）、混合題47–50共10分（47–48填充各2分、49多選4分且8個選項(A)–(H)、50簡答2分）、非選擇題28分（中譯英2題各4分、英文作文20分、至少120個單詞）；考試時間100分鐘。第49題官方答案 DF 與 spec by_year.112 記載一致。

第47、48題：題本共用一段作答說明與一個句子（題號印為「47-48」），兩題的 stem 都放入完整說明與句子，空格寫成 [[47]]、[[48]]；配分依題末「（填充，4分）」與評分原則「完全正確得2分」每格2分。評分原則的參考答案表格為兩欄成對答案（47 taste／48 health，或 47 health／48 taste），answer 取第一欄（47 taste、48 health），另一欄放 accepted_answers；兩格必須是一組（不可兩格填同一字），此限制寫在 scoring_notes。

第47、48、50題（混合題非選擇作答）及中譯英、作文：大考中心沒有公布逐題答對率／鑑別度，stats 為 null。stats-3.xls 只提供「第一題（滿分8分）＝中譯英兩小題合計」與「第二題（滿分20分）＝英文作文」的分數人數分布，以擴充欄位放在大題層級 sections[s7].stats、sections[s8].stats（range／count／percent／cum_count／cum_percent，百分比已除以100；分母為報考人數 118,185，含缺考 2,266）。

第49題（多選）：依統計表備註「題號前有『*』符號者為多選題，以得分率代替答對率」，correct_rate 填得分率 0.38，另以擴充欄位 full_correct_rate 記錄全對率 T＝0.07；option_rates 為各選項被劃記比例（可複選），加總約 2.56 > 1 屬正常（validator 的加總 warning 由此而來）。options 只放留言者姓名（A Olivia … H Alexander），留言全文在 s6g1.passage_parts。

stats 除 schema 欄位外另加（與 gsat-114 相同）：option_rates_high／option_rates_low（高分組前33%、低分組後33%的選項選答比例）、no_answer_rate（全體未答比例）、five_groups（Pa–Pe 五個能力組答對率）；未收 D1–D4。第30、35題低分組各有 1% 未答、第49題低分組有 4% 未答（全體 2%），no_answer_rate 只記全體（T 列）而未另列高低分組。
統計異常照錄：第4題（bare）官方鑑別度為負（D＝−0.06，高分組答對率 0.23 低於低分組 0.29；高分組有 36% 選 (A) blank、37% 選 (C) hollow）；第7題答對率僅 0.23。數值照官方填入，未調整。

中譯英參考答案：評分原則以大括號並列可替換寫法。第1題 History {proves / has proven / has proved} {time and again / repeatedly} that wars will {cause / lead to} extremely {terrible / horrible} disasters. —— answer 取各括號第一個寫法，其餘 23 種組合放 accepted_answers。第2題 {To avoid / Avoiding} conflicts and {ensure / ensuring} world peace should be … —— 兩組括號是平行結構，只展開「To avoid … and ensure …」（answer）與「Avoiding … and ensuring …」（accepted_answers）兩種；交叉組合（To avoid … ensuring／Avoiding … ensure）不合平行結構，評分原則版面雖未明示配對，仍不列入。原始大括號寫法逐字保留在 scoring_notes。
中譯英題號沿用題本 1、2（label「中譯英1」「中譯英2」），作文題本無題號，填 no=1、label「英文作文」，因此與詞彙題 1、2 題號重複（validator「題號重複 [1, 2]」warning 屬預期），label 皆不重複。
第參部分（非選擇題）的部分說明「說明：本部分共有二大題，…作答時不必抄題。」放在 sections[s7].part_instructions（擴充欄位，與 gsat-115 相同），s7.instructions 只放中譯英本身的說明。第壹部分標題「第壹部分、選擇題（占62分）」以 part＝「選擇題」表示，未另存。
作文：scoring_notes 收錄評分原則前言中關於作文的說明、評分原則全文與「表一、英文作文評分指標」（表格依「項目：等級（分數）描述」轉成文字）；官方沒有範文，answer 為 null。四個表情符號圖片（無文字說明）依頁面影像描述於 s8g1.figures，essay_type 標 picture。
第44題：選項為地圖上的圓圈代號 A–D，地圖內容依頁面影像描述於 s5g3.figures（kind＝map；描述只寫圖上位置，不寫國名對應與答案，避免顯示給學生時洩題）；題組選文本身為連續文本，text_format 仍標 continuous（與 gsat-115 第38題地圖選項的處理一致），item_type 標 chart_reading。

格式：題本的粗體不保留——第37題「NOT」（原文即大寫）、混合題引言「But do the customers really like them?」、47–48 說明「每格限填一個單詞（word）」、第49題「only under certain circumstances」、第50題「phrase」皆為粗體。例外：第42題問 “it” in the last paragraph，選文最後一段有三個 it（Is it possible／make it possible／doing it right），題本以粗體標出所問的是「make it possible」的 it，為免學生作答時無法辨識，比照 gsat-110（粗體標示的 they、ultra-accessible）在選文中以 <u>it</u> 標出（查證者修正）；第42題題幹本身以引號標示 “it”，不加 <u>。

原文照錄、未更正：第35題選項 (A)「hula-hooping」（選文寫作「hula hooping」，無連字號）；第50題題幹在 “works well” 與問號之間有一個空格（「“works well” ?」，PDF 與 Word 版皆同）；第49題問號後空一格再接「（多選題，4分）」照 Word 版保留。選文中的上標序數（18th、14th、8th、12th、15th、16th）改為一般文字。
空格表示：詞彙題空格統一寫成「______」（第4題題本原文即為底線字元）；綜合測驗、文意選填、篇章結構、混合題 47–48 的空格寫成 [[題號]]。第9題 Word 版在空格前有強制換行，已合併為同一句。

標註：sdgs 只在主題明確相關時填（水分補充與健康 3；茶園危害亞洲象 12、15；植物肉的健康與消費 3、12）；第18題 grammar_point 標 participle（四個選項為 redistribute／redistributed／redistributing／being redistributed，句構為「主要動詞＋分詞構句 shifting …」，需判斷空格應為主要動詞）；篇章結構 31 標 contrast（used to be accused … however）、32 標 pronoun_reference（This consistency 指前句 persistently give the same answer）、33、34 標 example（空格後分別接 For example 與 As is often observed 的例證）；第49題 item_type 標 inference（判斷誰「只在特定情況下」會選擇 GreenBurger：Thomas once in a while、Linda 待價格降低）。

查證（verifier）獨立核對結果：①第1–46、49題答案逐題對照 answer.pdf，全部一致；47、48、50 參考答案與 scoring.pdf 頁面影像一致。②全部題幹、選項、文意選填 A–J 與篇章結構 A–D 選項庫、7 篇選文與混合題引言／8 則留言，以程式與 Word 版（paper-2.docx）逐字比對完全一致，並與 pdftotext -layout 擷取的 PDF 文字逐詞比對，只有上標「18 th」與換行斷字「fakey-／fakey」兩處排版差異；選文段落數（3/2/3/5/4/3/4）依頁面影像首行縮排確認，詞數（211/221/304/296/292/306/350，含 [[題號]]）與 PDF 一致，[[題號]] 位置正確。③第44題地圖、作文四個表情符號以 250dpi／200dpi 頁面影像放大確認描述正確；地圖描述原含「約坦尚尼亞外海」與「官方答案為 B」，會在顯示給學生時洩題，已改為只描述圖上位置。④統計以程式重讀 stats-1/2.xls，47 題的 P、Ph、Pl、D、Pa–Pe、T（第49題全對率）、T/H/L 選項比例與未答率共 424 個欄位全部與 JSON 一致，* 號選項與官方答案一致；stats-3.xls 兩題分數分布（10 列／22 列）全部一致。⑤中譯英題目、作文提示、評分原則（含大括號參考答案與表一評分指標）對照 scoring.pdf 頁面影像逐字一致；中譯英1 的 24 種組合完整。⑥修正：第42題選文粗體 it 加 <u>；第44題地圖描述移除洩題文字並補記澳洲輪廓；統計 issue 補記第49題低分組未答 4%。
